issues.description: PaymentDetails interface exposes sensitive credit card data (cardNumber, cvv) in plaintext without any indication of encryption or PCI compliance
issues.suggestion: Never handle raw credit card data in application code. Use a PCI-compliant payment gateway (Stripe, PayPal) with tokenization. Store only tokens, not raw card details.

issues.description: Credit card number is logged/stored in database query with payment.cardNumber.slice(-4), but the full cardNumber is passed around in the PaymentDetails object throughout the application
issues.suggestion: Remove cardNumber, cvv, and expiryDate from the PaymentDetails interface entirely. Integrate with a payment processor API that handles tokenization and returns only a payment token.

issues.description: Card number validation only checks length === 16, missing Luhn algorithm validation and not accounting for cards with 13-19 digits
issues.suggestion: Use a proven payment validation library or remove card validation entirely by delegating to a PCI-compliant payment gateway. If validation is needed, implement Luhn algorithm: const isValid = (num) => { let sum = 0, isEven = false; for (let i = num.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) { let digit = parseInt(num[i]); if (isEven) digit *= 2; if (digit > 9) digit -= 9; sum += digit; isEven = !isEven; } return sum % 10 === 0; }

issues.description: Date comparison for card expiry uses 2000 + parseInt(year) which will break in year 2100, and the comparison uses < instead of <= causing cards to appear valid on their expiry month
issues.suggestion: Fix date logic: const currentDate = new Date(); const expiryDateObj = new Date(2000 + parseInt(year), parseInt(month)); if (expiryDateObj <= currentDate) { return false; }. Consider using a more robust date library or full 4-digit years.

issues.description: hasFeatureAccess returns false when db.query throws an error (unhandled promise rejection), causing silent failures in authorization checks
issues.suggestion: Add explicit error handling: try { const rows = await db.query(query, [userId]); if (rows.length === 0) return false; // ... rest of logic } catch (error) { console.error('Feature access check failed:', error); throw new Error('Unable to verify feature access'); }

issues.description: JSON.parse(subscription.features) can throw if the database contains invalid JSON, causing the function to crash
issues.suggestion: Add try-catch around JSON.parse: try { const features = JSON.parse(subscription.features); return features.includes(feature); } catch (error) { console.error('Invalid features JSON:', error); return false; }

issues.description: getUserSubscription has unhandled JSON.parse that can throw if database contains malformed JSON
issues.suggestion: Wrap JSON.parse in try-catch: try { return { userId: row.user_id, tier: row.tier, validUntil: new Date(row.valid_until), features: JSON.parse(row.features) }; } catch (error) { console.error('Failed to parse subscription:', error); return null; }

issues.description: processPremiumPayment does not handle the case where upgradeUserSubscription fails after payment succeeds, leading to charged users without upgraded subscriptions
issues.suggestion: Wrap in transaction or add compensating logic: try { await upgradeUserSubscription(userId, tier); } catch (error) { await refundPayment(payment, amount); throw new Error('Subscription upgrade failed, payment refunded'); }

issues.description: Error logging with console.error('Payment failed:', error) may expose sensitive payment details or database connection strings in logs
issues.suggestion: Log only safe error information: console.error('Payment failed for user', { timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), errorCode: error.code }); Avoid logging full error objects that may contain sensitive data.

issues.description: hasFeatureAccess makes a database query on every feature check without caching, causing performance issues for frequently checked features
issues.suggestion: Implement caching: const cache = new Map(); export async function hasFeatureAccess(userId: string, feature: string): Promise<boolean> { const cacheKey = `${userId}:${feature}`; if (cache.has(cacheKey)) return cache.get(cacheKey); const result = await checkFeatureInDB(userId, feature); cache.set(cacheKey, result); setTimeout(() => cache.delete(cacheKey), 60000); return result; }

issues.description: Feature arrays are duplicated with magic string values in upgradeUserSubscription, making it hard to maintain and prone to typos
issues.suggestion: Extract to constants: const PREMIUM_FEATURES = ['unlimited_todos', 'priority_support', 'custom_themes']; const ENTERPRISE_FEATURES = [...PREMIUM_FEATURES, 'api_access', 'team_collaboration']; const features = tier === 'premium' ? PREMIUM_FEATURES : ENTERPRISE_FEATURES;

issues.description: Magic numbers for TAX_RATE and PROCESSING_FEE are hardcoded in calculateSubscriptionPrice, making them difficult to update or configure
issues.suggestion: Move to configuration: const CONFIG = { TAX_RATE: 0.08, PROCESSING_FEE: 0.029 }; Or accept as parameters if they vary by region: function calculateSubscriptionPrice(tier: string, taxRate = 0.08, processingFee = 0.029)

issues.description: Card number validation doesn't check if cardNumber contains only digits, allowing letters or special characters
issues.suggestion: Add digit validation: if (!/^\d{13,19}$/.test(cardNumber.replace(/\s/g, ''))) { return false; }

issues.description: Direct comparison validUntil < new Date() creates a new Date object on each comparison, slightly inefficient
issues.suggestion: Create date once: const now = new Date(); if (validUntil < now) { return false; }

codeQuality.summary: Critical security issues with handling raw credit card data violating PCI compliance standards, multiple high-severity bug risks including unhandled promise rejections and JSON parsing errors, and lack of transaction handling for payment processing. The code requires immediate security remediation before production use.

testCoverage.summary: No test file exists for src/premium.ts. This file contains critical payment processing, card validation, pricing calculation, and subscription management logic with zero test coverage. refactorings.summary: The premium.ts file contains critical payment and subscription logic that would benefit from extracting testable functions, simplifying validation flows with guard clauses, and creating reusable utilities. The highest-impact refactorings focus on extracting feature configuration, expiry validation, and subscription validity checks into separate functions to improve testability and reduce duplication. Additional improvements include simplifying calculations and maintaining consistent formatting for early returns.

recommendations.description: Replace raw credit card handling with PCI-compliant payment gateway tokenization (Stripe, PayPal) to avoid storing sensitive card data.
Add comprehensive test coverage for payment processing function including validation, charging, and subscription upgrade paths.
Add test coverage for card validation logic including card number, CVV, and expiry date validation edge cases.
Add test coverage for pricing calculation logic to ensure correct calculation of base price, tax, and processing fees for all tiers.
Add test coverage for payment gateway integration including successful charges and database error handling.
Implement Luhn algorithm validation for card numbers or delegate all validation to payment gateway to ensure card number validity.
Add error handling for database queries and JSON parsing operations to prevent unhandled promise rejections and crashes.
Add test coverage for subscription upgrade logic including feature assignment, validity period, and existing subscription updates.
Add test coverage for feature access control including expiry validation and feature inclusion checks.
Implement transaction handling or compensating logic to prevent charging users without upgrading their subscriptions.
